Te berekenen
Mogelijke meetpunten
Deelname, volhouden, welzijn, fitheid, blessures, plezier, uitval en kosten — meetmethoden nog te bepalen
Stopcriteria en evaluatie
Vooraf te bepalen, inclusief ongewenste effecten
04 / Kosten
Wat vraagt dit aan middelen?
Dit is de structuur voor een kostenmodel. De bedragen, volumes en aannames moeten nog worden uitgewerkt; er is nog geen begroting.
05 / Bewijs
Onderbouwing vóór overtuiging.
Wat we al weten

Er zijn nog geen geverifieerde onderzoeksbronnen aan dit bouwplan toegevoegd. Daarom geven we hier geen wetenschappelijke conclusies over gezondheidseffecten, deelname of verplichting. Dat jongeren de mogelijkheid moeten krijgen om passend te bewegen is ons uitgangspunt. Of dit kader werkt en welke deelnamevorm te rechtvaardigen is, moet nog worden onderbouwd.
Wat we nog moeten bewijzen
Kritiek & risico’s
Een goed bouwplan moet kritiek kunnen verdragen.
Dit zijn open vragen, geen bezwaren waarvoor al een antwoord klaarligt. Ze moeten onderdeel zijn van het onderzoek en van de beslissing om wel of niet te testen.
06 / Resultaten
Nog geen resultaten.

Er is nog geen BOUW-pilot uitgevoerd. Hier komen later gemeten uitkomsten met meetmethoden, bronverwijzingen en beperkingen, inclusief blessures, uitval en ervaringen van jongeren. Ook nulresultaten of nadelige effecten moeten zichtbaar worden. Nu zijn er geen resultaten die dit voorstel of sportplicht rechtvaardigen.
07 / Volgende stap
Van idee naar pilot.

Eerst bepalen wat een verantwoord onderzoek moet toetsen. Een toegankelijke beweegbasis ontwerpen en de vraag naar verplichting onderzoeken zijn verschillende stappen. Pas na onderbouwing en evaluatie kan worden besloten of het idee verder verdient te gaan.
Daag dit voorstel uit
Wat zien we over het hoofd?
Een bouwplan wordt beter door kritiek, niet door kritiek te vermijden.

title: Onze visie — BOUW
headings: Nederland hoeft problemen niet alleen te beheren.We kunnen oplossingen bouwen.
Een overtuiging is nog geen uitkomst.
Maak de basis overvloediger en betaalbaarder. Geef mensen daarna meer ruimte om hun eigen leven te bouwen.
content: Onze visie / Geen beloftes. Bouwplannen.
Nederland hoeft problemen niet alleen te beheren.We kunnen oplossingen bouwen.

BOUW kiest voor een land dat ideeën uitwerkt, onzekerheid erkent en in de praktijk onderzoekt wat werkt. Onze overtuigingen geven richting. Bewijs moet laten zien welke oplossingen die richting werkelijk dichterbij brengen.
Niet links tegen rechts.Niet optimisme tegen pessimisme.Bouwen tegen stilstaan.
Conceptbeeld / een mogelijke toekomst
Ambitie met open ogen
Een overtuiging is nog geen uitkomst.
We maken zichtbaar wat we geloven, waar we naartoe willen en wat nog onderzocht moet worden.
Principes
Wat BOUW fundamenteel gelooft. Een overtuiging is geen bewijs van een effect.
Standpunten
De richting waarin we Nederland willen bewegen. Geen uitgewerkt pakket maatregelen.
Voorstellen
Concrete mechanismen die we nog moeten onderzoeken, doorrekenen en toetsen.
Projecten
Systemen en concepten die we kunnen ontwerpen, ontwikkelen en testen.
Resultaten
Wat daadwerkelijk is gemeten en aangetoond, met bronnen en beperkingen. Op deze site zijn nog geen BOUW-pilotresultaten gepubliceerd.
Principes / Vier pijlers
Waar we op bouwen.
Dit zijn overtuigingen over de richting die we kiezen. Hoe we die waarmaken, moet zorgvuldig worden uitgewerkt en getoetst.
01 / Principe
Gezonde mensen
Een sterke samenleving begint met mensen die de basis hebben om goed te leven.
Dagelijkse maaltijden of beweegverwachtingen zijn mogelijke uitwerkingen. Hun vorm en werking staan nog niet vast.
02 / Principe
Een land dat bouwt
Nederland moet weer het vertrouwen krijgen om te bouwen wat het nodig heeft.
Ambitie vraagt om uitvoerbare plannen. Snelheid, betaalbaarheid en leefbaarheid moeten samen worden onderzocht.
03 / Principe
Meer vrijheid door een sterke basis
Vrijheid betekent meer als de basis niet je hele leven opeist.

BOUW bouwt mogelijkheden, geen verplichtingen. Een goed systeem geeft mensen meer keuzes over hun eigen leven — niet minder. De vrijheidstest onderzoekt onnodige dwang naast werking, kosten en gevolgen.
04 / Principe
Proberen. Meten. Verbeteren.
Overheid en samenleving moeten beter worden in het erkennen van onzekerheid.
Mislukken mag. Verbergen niet.
Een bouwplan beoordelen
De vrijheidstest
Geeft dit mensen meer zeggenschap over hun eigen leven, of minder?

Een oplossing die technisch werkt maar onnodig vrijheid wegneemt, is nog geen goed bouwplan. We toetsen bewijs, haalbaarheid, kosten, risico’s, resultaten én persoonlijke zeggenschap — ook wanneer onze eigen ideeën daardoor afvallen.

Overheid en samenleving hebben verantwoordelijkheden voor wetgeving, veiligheid, infrastructuur en gezamenlijke voorzieningen. De toets vraagt of een beperking noodzakelijk en proportioneel is, en of een vrijer alternatief hetzelfde doel kan bereiken.
Standpunten / Onze richting
Wat we willen veranderen.
Twaalf richtingen, met ruimte voor onderzoek. De doelen geven koers; de uitwerking is geen vaststaand beleid.
De basis om goed te leven.
Standpunt / Gewenste richting
Verse, voedzame voeding hoort geen luxe te zijn. BOUW wil onderzoeken hoe productie, technologie, kortere ketens en meer aanbod de werkelijke kosten kunnen verlagen.
Uitwerking / Nog te onderzoeken
Lokale productie is niet automatisch goedkoper. Investeringen, energie, importalternatieven en de verdeling van eventuele besparingen moeten worden meegewogen.
Standpunt / Gewenste richting

De toegang van jongeren tot voedzame voeding zou niet volledig afhankelijk moeten zijn van het huishoudinkomen. Een gegarandeerde voedingsbasis verdient onderzoek, beginnend met een toetsbaar pilotontwerp.
Uitwerking / Nog te onderzoeken
Samenstelling, toegang, universele of gerichte ondersteuning, uitvoering en kosten zijn nog open vragen. Er is geen BOUW-pilot gestart.
Standpunt / Gewenste richting
We willen meer woningen en meer ruimte voor leefbare buurten. Snellere, betaalbaardere manieren van bouwen, waaronder modulaire modellen, moeten worden ontwikkeld en getest.
Uitwerking / Nog te onderzoeken
We presenteren geen bewezen bouwtempo of kostenbesparing. Kwaliteit, infrastructuur en leefbaarheid horen bij de toetsing.
Standpunt / Gewenste richting
Sport en lichamelijke ontwikkeling verdienen een veel sterkere plek in het opgroeien. Het doel is gezondheid en mogelijkheden, met ruimte voor verschillen tussen jongeren.
Uitwerking / Nog te onderzoeken

De balans tussen stimulering, toegankelijkheid, verwachtingen en verplichting is nog te onderzoeken. Sportplicht is geen vastgesteld BOUW-beleid. De vrijheidstest stelt een hogere eis: noodzaak, bewijs, proportionaliteit, alternatieven en gevolgen voor rechten en vrijheid. Dit onderzoek kan de verplichtingsoptie ook verwerpen.
Een land dat mogelijkheden maakt.
Standpunt / Gewenste richting

Bouw, technologie, landbouw, maakindustrie en andere praktische vaardigheden verdienen respect als serieuze routes naar een goede toekomst. We willen dat leren maken en vakmanschap volwaardig meetellen.
Uitwerking / Nog te onderzoeken
Welke onderwijs- en ontwikkelroutes daarbij passen, moet met aandacht voor jongeren, onderwijskwaliteit en uitvoerbaarheid worden uitgewerkt.
Standpunt / Gewenste richting
Productief werk, vaardigheden leren en ondernemen moeten een geloofwaardige route vormen naar meer zelfstandigheid en een beter leven.
Uitwerking / Nog te onderzoeken
Dit is een richting, geen belofte over inkomens of koopkracht. Concrete maatregelen vragen een kostenplaatje en onderzoek naar hun gevolgen.
Standpunt / Gewenste richting
Grijp eerder in. BOUW wil voorkomen dat beheersbare financiële problemen uitgroeien tot langdurige persoonlijke en maatschappelijke schade.
Uitwerking / Nog te onderzoeken
Hoe preventie, kennis en begeleiding kunnen werken, moet worden uitgewerkt en getoetst. Er zijn nog geen resultaten van een BOUW-schuldenprogramma.
08 / Standpunt
BOUW wil onderzoeken of Nederland een belangrijk knooppunt kan worden voor voedzame plantaardige producten van Nederlandse én internationale boeren en telers.

De richting: een sterke, eerlijke opbrengst voor boeren en telers verbinden aan een ruim aanbod van verse, voedzame producten. We willen onderzoeken of die combinatie gezond eten bereikbaar kan maken voor jongeren. Een goede vergoeding, voldoende aanbod en lage consumentenprijzen gaan niet vanzelf samen; het volledige model moet worden doorgerekend.

Een mogelijke uitwerking is toegang tot een voedzame, verse maaltijd overdag voor jongeren van ongeveer 13–17 jaar, vooral tijdens het voortgezet onderwijs. Die leeftijdsgroep, het maaltijdconcept, de toegang en de financiering zijn voorstellen om te onderzoeken, geen vastgesteld programma.

Daarnaast willen we verkennen hoe voeding, lichamelijke ontwikkeling, onderwijs en voorbereiding op praktisch vakwerk elkaar kunnen versterken. Dat vraagt om zorgvuldig ontwikkelde onderwijs- en leerwerktrajecten, niet om jongeren simpelweg van school te laten vertrekken.
Voorstellen / Nog te onderzoeken

BOUW betaalt nu geen boeren, importeert geen voedsel en voert geen maaltijdprogramma uit. Er zijn geen afspraken met scholen. Economische haalbaarheid, voedingskundige onderbouwing, verantwoordelijkheden en uitvoering moeten nog worden onderzocht.

Een toekomstig traject moet binnen de bestaande leerplicht en, waar van toepassing, kwalificatieplicht passen en juridisch en onderwijskundig worden ontwikkeld. Dit voorstel betekent niet dat een 13-jarige school kan verlaten om voor BOUW te werken.
Vooruitgang die zich laat toetsen.
Standpunt / Gewenste richting

AI, automatisering, biotechnologie en engineering moeten menselijke mogelijkheden, overvloed en kwaliteit van leven vergroten. We willen technologie beoordelen op wat zij mensen oplevert, voorbij alleen extra productiviteit.
Uitwerking / Nog te onderzoeken
Mogelijke toepassingen vragen onderzoek naar werking, veiligheid, vrijheid en gevolgen. Een technisch idee is nog geen bewezen verbetering.
Standpunt / Gewenste richting
Waar dat praktisch kan, moeten grote nieuwe interventies beginnen met meetbare pilots. Bepaal vooraf wat we willen leren, wat het kost en wanneer doorgaan, aanpassen of stoppen gerechtvaardigd is.
Uitwerking / Nog te onderzoeken
Een kleine proef is geen automatisch bewijs dat landelijke invoering werkt. Schaal, context en beperkingen moeten onderdeel blijven van de beoordeling.
Standpunt / Gewenste richting
Publiceer mislukkingen en negatieve resultaten naast successen. Een mislukt experiment kan iets leren; verbergen maakt eerlijke beoordeling onmogelijk.
Uitwerking / Nog te onderzoeken
Dit is onze norm voor toekomstige tests. We claimen hiermee geen al uitgevoerde onderzoeken of gepubliceerde pilotresultaten.
Standpunt / Gewenste richting
Beoordeel ideeën op bewijs, gevolgen, haalbaarheid, vrijheid en resultaten. Hun traditionele plek aan de linker- of rechterkant van de politiek hoort niet te bepalen of we ze serieus onderzoeken.
Uitwerking / Nog te onderzoeken
Constructief bouwen vraagt ook dat we onze eigen aannames kunnen herzien. Een aantrekkelijk idee moet kritiek en toetsing kunnen verdragen.
Bouwen tegen stilstaan
Maak de basis overvloediger en betaalbaarder. Geef mensen daarna meer ruimte om hun eigen leven te bouwen.

title: Standpunten — BOUW
headings: Een gezonde basis moet bereikbaar zijn.
Bouw aan wat mensen nodig hebben.
Van richting naar een toetsbaar plan.
content: Waar we voor bouwen
Standpunten
Geen lijst met beloftes voor over vier jaar. Dit is de richting waarin BOUW Nederland wil bewegen — en de ideeën die we willen onderzoeken om daar te komen.
Overtuiging is nog geen bewijs
Richting kiezen. Uitvoering onderzoeken.
StandpuntRichting
Waar BOUW Nederland naartoe wil bewegen. Een overtuiging, geen bewezen maatregel.
VoorstelIn onderzoek
Een mogelijke uitvoering. Aannames, kosten, gevolgen en alternatieven moeten nog worden onderzocht.
PilotPilot nodig
Een volgende onderzoeksstap, zodra het plan toetsbaar genoeg is. Dit label betekent niet dat er al een proef loopt.
Resultaat
Een daadwerkelijk gemeten uitkomst, met methode, bronnen en beperkingen. Er zijn nog geen BOUW-pilotresultaten gepubliceerd op deze site.
01—04 / Goed opgroeien
Een gezonde basis moet bereikbaar zijn.
01 / Standpunt
Vers eten moet goedkoper
Verse, voedzame plantaardige voeding moet veel betaalbaarder worden. Gezond eten hoort niet de luxe optie te zijn.
In onderzoek Mogelijke uitwerking

BOUW onderzoekt of meer aanbod van Nederlandse en internationale telers, kastechnologie, efficiënte logistiek, kortere ketens waar zinvol en minder verspilling de werkelijke kosten kunnen verlagen. Voor huishoudens voor wie gezond eten dan nog moeilijk betaalbaar blijft, willen we onderzoeken of ondersteuning kan meebewegen met het huishoudinkomen.

Lokale productie is niet automatisch goedkoper. Volledige kosten, importalternatieven en wie eventuele besparingen ontvangt, blijven open vragen. Inkomensafhankelijke ondersteuning is geen vastgesteld systeem.
02 / Standpunt
Goed eten voor jongeren die bouwen aan hun toekomst
Jongeren moeten kunnen leren, zich ontwikkelen en werken zonder de dag met honger door te komen.
In onderzoek Mogelijke uitwerking

We willen toegang tot verse, voedzame maaltijden onderzoeken voor jongeren in de middelbareschoolleeftijd en voor jongeren in toekomstige, erkende praktische leer- en werktrajecten. Wie in aanmerking komt, welke leeftijden passend zijn, hoe het wordt betaald en hoe de maaltijd wordt aangeboden, staan nog open.
BOUW voert geen maaltijdprogramma uit en heeft geen afspraken met scholen of leerwerkorganisaties. Eventuele trajecten moeten onderwijskundig en juridisch worden ontwikkeld.
03 / Standpunt
Een persoonlijk voedselpakket
Ondersteuning bij gezond eten moet eenvoudig, passend en toegankelijk kunnen zijn. Een voedingsbasis hoeft niet voor iedereen hetzelfde pakket te betekenen.
In onderzoek Mogelijke uitwerking

Een mogelijke uitwerking is een eenvoudig overheidssysteem waarmee mensen die in aanmerking komen terugkerende pakketten verse plantaardige producten kunnen ontvangen. De voorwaarden, samenstelling, financiering en uitvoering moeten nog worden onderzocht.

We onderzoeken als concept een nieuwe overheidsdienst met DigiD, waarmee iemand toegang tot een passend pakket zou kunnen regelen. Er is geen dienst gebouwd, geen DigiD-koppeling en geen overheidsafspraak. Ook een goed toegankelijk alternatief voor wie digitaal niet mee kan doen, moet worden onderzocht.

Dataminimalisatie is het uitgangspunt. Lengte, gewicht of gezondheidsinformatie verzamelen we niet alleen omdat dat mogelijk is. Zulke gegevens zijn gevoelig; noodzaak, privacy, beveiliging, bewaartermijnen en een passende juridische grondslag moeten eerst zorgvuldig worden uitgewerkt. Deze pagina vraagt of verzamelt geen persoonlijke gegevens.
04 / Standpunt
Bewegen hoort bij opgroeien
Lichamelijke ontwikkeling en regelmatig bewegen verdienen een normale, sterke plek in het opgroeien. Het doel is gezondheid en mogelijkheden, niet straf of uniforme prestaties.
In onderzoek Mogelijke uitwerking

Sport, wandelen, hardlopen, krachtontwikkeling, praktisch lichamelijk werk en andere toegankelijke activiteiten zijn mogelijke onderdelen. We willen ook onderzoeken of gestructureerde lichamelijke ontwikkeling kan passen binnen toekomstige praktische onderwijs- en werktrajecten. Een sportplicht of minimale deelnameverwachting kan worden onderzocht, maar is geen vastgesteld beleid. De vrijheidstest vraagt daarvoor een veel hogere drempel: noodzaak, bewijs, proportionaliteit, alternatieven en gevolgen voor rechten en vrijheid. Zonder sterke rechtvaardiging valt die optie af.

Gewoon schoolverzuim plaatst een kind niet automatisch in een BOUW-programma. Er is geen programma of plaatsingsregeling. Keuzevrijheid, passende begeleiding en juridische en onderwijskundige toetsing moeten vooraf worden uitgewerkt.
Nederland draait al.
Dus misschien moeten we minder vragen hoe we Nederland draaiende houden — en meer hoe we het beter laten draaien.
05 / Standpunt
Nederland als knooppunt voor plantaardig voedsel

BOUW wil onderzoeken of Nederland een uitzonderlijk internationaal knooppunt kan worden voor voedzame plantaardige producten. Een sterke, eerlijke opbrengst voor telers moet samengaan met ruimere toegang tot goed eten hier.
In onderzoek Mogelijke uitwerking

We willen de mogelijkheden van logistiek, havens, landbouw, kaskennis, voedseltechnologie en internationale handel verkennen, samen met de mogelijke rol van Nederlandse én internationale boeren en telers. De vraag is hoe een groot en betrouwbaar aanbod gezond eten eenvoudiger en betaalbaarder kan maken, zonder een goede vergoeding voor producenten uit het oog te verliezen.

Het gaat om een systeem om te onderzoeken, niet alleen om meer import. BOUW heeft geen telersovereenkomsten, importprogramma’s of operationele voedselinfrastructuur. LOOP en GROW zijn concepten, geen bewijs dat deze keten al bestaat.
06—10 / Meer ruimte om te leven
Bouw aan wat mensen nodig hebben.
06 / Standpunt
Warmte moet betaalbaar zijn
Huishoudelijke warmte moet betaalbaar blijven. De manier waarop moet ook op gezondheid, veiligheid en gevolgen voor de omgeving worden beoordeeld.
In onderzoek Mogelijke uitwerking

We willen onderzoeken of haarden, moderne houtverwarming en verantwoord gewonnen brandhout voor sommige huishoudens een bruikbare rol kunnen spelen. Mogelijke ideeën zijn het verlagen of wegnemen van bepaalde belastingen op geschikte apparatuur bij aantoonbaar publiek voordeel, en betere toegang tot betaalbaar, verantwoord gewonnen hout. Geen van deze maatregelen is vastgesteld.

Dit is geen stookadvies of voorstel dat houtverwarming overal geschikt verklaart. Gezondheidsrisico’s en effecten voor omwonenden horen vanaf het begin bij het onderzoek. ‘Belastingvrije haarden’ is geen BOUW-beleid.
07 / Standpunt
Praktisch leren is echt onderwijs
Wie tot zijn recht komt door te bouwen, repareren, telen, koken, ontwerpen of maken, verdient een serieuze onderwijsroute naar volwassenheid. Vakmanschap hoort echte status te hebben.
In onderzoek Mogelijke uitwerking

We willen erkende routes verkennen waarin onderwijs, vakmanschap, beweging, goede voeding en praktijkervaring elkaar versterken. Welke begeleiding, kwaliteitseisen en verantwoordelijkheden daarbij horen, moet nog worden ontwikkeld.

Een toekomstig traject moet binnen de bestaande leerplicht en, waar van toepassing, kwalificatieplicht worden ontworpen. Als verandering van onderwijsregels nodig zou zijn, moet die uitdrukkelijk juridisch en democratisch worden uitgewerkt. Dit is geen toestemming voor 13-jarigen om school te verlaten, en BOUW biedt nu geen erkend traject aan.
08 / Standpunt
Bouw totdat wonen weer normaal wordt
We willen schaarste aan woningen aanpakken door veel meer te bouwen, met aandacht voor betaalbaarheid en leefbare buurten.
In onderzoek Mogelijke uitwerking

Modulaire bouw, snellere methoden, alternatieve buurtmodellen, kleinere betaalbare woningen en nieuwe materialen en productietechnieken verdienen ontwikkeling en toetsing. Kwaliteit, infrastructuur en volledige kosten moeten onderdeel zijn van de afweging.
HIVE verkent dit als woonconcept. Het is niet operationeel en er zijn geen aangetoonde bouwtempo’s, gerealiseerde woningen of besparingen van BOUW.
09 / Standpunt
Pak schulden aan voordat ze levens beheersen
Kleine financiële problemen mogen niet onnodig uitgroeien tot jarenlange schade. Herstel moet mogelijk zijn.
In onderzoek Mogelijke uitwerking

BOUW wil eerder ingrijpen, eenvoudigere routes uit problematische schulden verkennen en systemen onderzoeken die herstel ondersteunen. Kennis en begeleiding zijn mogelijke onderdelen; werking en kosten moeten worden getoetst.
RISE is een concept om te ontwikkelen, geen bestaande hulpdienst. Er zijn geen gemeten resultaten van een BOUW-schuldenprogramma.
10 / Standpunt
Werken moet weer iets opleveren
Wie nuttige vaardigheden leert, werkt en bijdraagt, moet een geloofwaardig pad naar zelfstandigheid hebben.
In onderzoek Mogelijke uitwerking

We willen onderzoeken hoe belastingen, toeslagen, woonlasten en andere systemen op elkaar inwerken, zodat meer verdienen ook daadwerkelijk ruimte in iemands leven kan geven. De effecten moeten per situatie worden bekeken.
Dit is een richting voor onderzoek. Er is in dit standpunt geen specifiek belastingplan, berekende koopkrachtwinst of vastgestelde maatregel.
11—13 / Open ogen, betere ideeën
Vooruitgang moet zich laten toetsen.
11 / Standpunt
Technologie moet mensen sterker maken

AI, automatisering, biotechnologie, engineering en nieuwe productiemethoden moeten menselijke mogelijkheden en overvloed vergroten. Technologie hoort meer op te leveren dan alleen extra productiviteit.
In onderzoek Mogelijke uitwerking

We willen toepassingen beoordelen op hun werking, gevolgen, veiligheid en bijdrage aan kwaliteit van leven. Technische mogelijkheden zijn een beginpunt voor onderzoek, geen garantie op maatschappelijk voordeel.
GROW en MEND zijn concepten waarin zulke vragen kunnen worden verkend. Speculatieve toepassingen, vooral rond gezondheid en biotechnologie, zijn geen bewezen technologieën of behandelingen.
12 / Standpunt
Eerst proberen. Dan meten. Dan opschalen.
Waar dat praktisch kan, moeten overheid en samenleving ideeën eerlijk testen voordat het hele land eraan wordt verbonden.
In onderzoek Mogelijke uitwerking

Een plan moet vooraf duidelijk maken wat we willen leren, wat succes betekent, wat het kost en wanneer we aanpassen of stoppen. Een pilot is een onderzoeksstap; een positief resultaat in één context rechtvaardigt niet automatisch landelijke invoering.
Probleem → Bouwplan → Pilot → Meten → Publiceren → Verbeteren → Opschalen of stoppen
Publiceer ook tegenvallers, negatieve uitkomsten en beperkingen. Onze voorstellen hebben nog geen BOUW-pilotresultaten; eerst moeten toetsbare ontwerpen worden uitgewerkt.

13 / Standpunt
Goede ideeën hebben geen politieke kleur
Begin niet met ‘Is dit links of rechts?’ Begin met ‘Werkt het?’
In onderzoek Mogelijke uitwerking

Beoordeel een idee op bewijs, gevolgen, haalbaarheid, betaalbaarheid, vrijheid en meetbare resultaten. We moeten onze eigen aannames kunnen herzien en ook een geliefd idee kunnen loslaten wanneer de onderbouwing ontbreekt.
Geen beloftes. Bouwplannen.
Van richting naar een toetsbaar plan.
Onze overtuigingen geven koers. De volgende stap is onderzoeken, doorrekenen en eerlijk toetsen wat werkelijk kan werken.

content: BOUWJAAR / early concept
BOUWJAAR
Discover what you can do. Find your own direction.

A good life takes more than knowing what you want to become. BOUWJAAR explores how young people could try practical skills, learn about health, take responsibility and work together — and discover possible directions.
Discovering possibilities
Learn by trying.
These themes are a direction to investigate, not a settled curriculum. Young people have different interests, abilities and circumstances. The design must make room for those differences.
Movement and physical capability
Find ways to move that suit you and discover what your body can do.
Food and cooking
Understand healthy food and learn to make simple meals.
Money and everyday finances
Learn about income, spending and financial choices.
Practical skills
Work with your hands, make things and solve problems.
Technology
Understand and try out tools and technology.
Teamwork and responsibility
Build something together, make agreements and take responsibility for your work.
Strengths and direction
Discover your strengths and what you want to explore next.
What we still need to work out
A clear direction. An open design.
Age, intended participants and how it fits with education remain questions to investigate.
The name is a working name. Duration, rhythm and setting have not been decided.
Voluntary participation, support and any expectations need investigation. No requirement to take part has been established.
Providers, guidance, expertise and responsibilities have not been chosen.
A curriculum, suitable adaptations and safety need to be developed with input from young people.
Funding, full costs, accessibility and evaluation remain open questions.
There is no programme, pilot, partnership, budget or measured result. Any possible pathway must fit with education and accommodate different physical and mental abilities.
Part of a larger story
More possibilities. Your own direction.

BOUWJAAR belongs near the beginning of BOUW’s framework for building a life. It is not military service or a path everyone must follow. A good design must give young people more control and room to choose a different direction.

The first step is to sharpen the questions: what do young people want to explore, what barriers exist, and what could be safe, accessible and practical? Only then could a responsible test be designed.

content: BOUW PROJECT / FOOD
LOOP
Fresh food. Regularly to your home.
LOOP explores whether fresh everyday food could reach households regularly. In the spirit of the old milkman, with modern local and regional production and distribution.
Status — In development
FROM RESEARCH TO PRODUCT
LOOP is now also being developed as a product experience.

LOOP is a project in development, not an operational food company or government programme. There are no LOOP hubs, distribution networks, supplier agreements, pilots or measured results. The hero image shows a possible atmosphere, not an established construction plan or existing LOOP location. Experiment 001 is in the model → kitchen-test phase; the model hypothesis is not a validated diet or measured weekly cost. LOOP owns no agricultural or greenhouse system and is not an investment product.
LOOP / the ambition
The milkman model. For tomorrow’s fresh food.
What problem are we examining?
How can fresh, nutritious food become affordable and convenient where people already live?
What is the idea?
A modern version of the milkman: food packages delivered regularly to households. A long-term ambition, not a chosen or proven distribution model.
How could it work?

Production → local or regional distribution → household food package → everyday meals. Use existing infrastructure where it works. Local growing and greenhouses near cities still need to demonstrate suitability and full costs.
What could everyday life look like?

If it worked, a household could regularly receive suitable fresh food and prepare its own meals. Contents, choice, price, frequency, refrigeration and delivery remain open. Collection or existing shops may prove better.

01 / Project model
The problem

Fresh food can be available in a country yet relatively expensive, hard to reach or inconveniently distributed within a particular community. LOOP first wants to establish where a meaningful access problem exists and what causes it, rather than choose the solution in advance.

Existing communities contain homes, family, work, relationships and history. The community is not the problem; food access, affordability and distribution are the research questions. This could be particularly relevant where fresh food is less accessible or relatively expensive, and for households where good food takes a substantial share of income or working time.

LOOP investigates an economically viable access system where possible. It is not emergency aid or a prescription for what people should eat, nor is it intended solely for one income group. Freedom of choice and local preferences belong in the design.
Conviction is not yet evidence.
02 / Project model
The aim
How do we bring affordable, fresh and nutritious food to people — without them having to move to access it?
A stronger food foundation, without having to move.

The ambition is to make nutritious food affordable and practically accessible where people already live. Lower costs are a possible means; better access is the aim. Good food can take less of your working time without making the producer's work less valuable.
Working hypothesis / still to be tested
This is a working hypothesis, not a proven causal chain. Every step must be tested. More supply, local production or fewer intermediaries do not guarantee a lower consumer price or better access.
03 / Project model
How LOOP could work

Producer → efficient distribution → local access point → household. Every step is open to testing. Use existing infrastructure when it works; build new infrastructure only when evidence shows it is needed. LOOP need not become its own supermarket chain or production company.
Producer

Independent farmers, Dutch and international growers, wholesalers and possibly future GROW concepts could be compared. LOOP investigates access, not ownership of large farms or greenhouses. Local cultivation and imports must be assessed on actual costs and suitability.
Efficient distribution

Investigate procurement, transport, storage, refrigeration, handling and waste across the whole chain. Coordinated demand or fewer intermediaries does not automatically save money. Producers must remain economically viable.
Local access point

A supermarket, neighbourhood shop, collection point or another model could form the final connection. Existing shops and infrastructure are fully valid possible solutions; no partners or locations have been established.
Household

People retain the choice of where they shop and what they eat. The system must fit everyday reality: preferences, accessibility, opening hours, affordability and freedom of choice. A food basket is a possible measurement unit, not a compulsory proprietary crate or final sales format.
04 / Project model
The local hub
What is the cheapest and simplest way to bring fresh food closer to people here?
A LOOP hub is a research concept, not a predetermined building. We must compare different formats for total costs and usability, including retaining existing amenities.
Still to be investigated. A test could also point to another solution. Building our own channel is not an aim in itself. If LOOP isn't needed somewhere, we won't build it there.
05 / Project model
How much of your life does good food cost?

Nominal prices remain necessary, but alone they do not show the human effort good food requires. LOOP wants to relate the price of a comparable nutritious weekly basket to a transparent local income or hourly earnings benchmark.
LOOP metric
How many hours must someone work for a week of fresh, nutritious food?

The basket, suitable regional substitutions and benchmark remain to be determined. Minimum wage where applicable, typical or median hourly earnings, or disposable household income translated into working time must be investigated for suitability. Units and assumptions must be explicit; never choose the benchmark that makes LOOP look best. Households, wages and purchasing power differ. One working hour does not mean the same everywhere, and equal working time does not mean equal prosperity. Comparable access for comparable effort remains long-term research, not a global promise.
06 / Project model
What must LOOP demonstrate?
Ambition is not yet evidence. First demonstrate the local problem, then compare a mechanism with what already exists. These questions are unanswered.
Does a meaningful food-access problem actually exist in the chosen test area?
Could a defined nutritious basket become easier to access?
Could the required working time fall substantially, using a fair benchmark?
Could that happen while producers receive economically viable compensation?
Would a local hub outperform ordinary supermarkets or existing shops?
Which distribution format has the lowest total costs?
Do convenience, distance and time improve alongside price?
Does food waste remain manageable?
Could the model function without permanent subsidy?
Are food baskets and regional substitutions actually comparable?

First prototype

Start deliberately small: one existing community, one comparable food basket, measure existing prices, calculate a working-time baseline and compare distribution formats. Only then a small access test and publication of results. No location, test group, supplier, budget or date has been chosen.

Do people actually choose the system, use the food and find it fits their preferences?
09 / Project model
What could go wrong?
A plan gets better through criticism, not by avoiding it. If LOOP isn't needed, not building is a meaningful outcome.
Challenge LOOP.
What are we missing?
10 / Project model
Results
No results yet.

No LOOP hub or completed LOOP pilot exists yet. No lower price, better access, reduction in required working time or producer return has been demonstrated. Once real measurements exist, unfavourable outcomes and limitations of the comparison belong here too.
11 / Project model
First the kitchen. Then further testing.

Experiment 001 begins with kitchen measurements of the model. Scientific review and investigation of procurement and logistics follow. For a later access test: identify a credible test area and establish the baseline: what does a week of fresh, nutritious food cost here today — in money and working time? Only then investigate whether another access model improves anything. The next step is not building a large LOOP complex.

GROW investigates production; LOOP investigates access and distribution. HIVE, as a research direction, builds a better foundation for new living environments; LOOP could bring part of that foundation to people already living somewhere. These are separate projects, not an existing integrated system. A future HIVE could use ordinary supermarkets or other food provision. People need not move to HIVE to benefit from better food access.
Proposal
A broader affordability question, still under investigation.
Production
Investigates possible production of nutritious plant-based food; no existing LOOP supplier.
Living environment
New complete living environments; LOOP focuses on access where people already live.

title: GROW — Food close to home — BOUW
content: BOUW PROJECT / FOOD PRODUCTION
Status — In development
GROW
The same mission. A different system for every climate.
GROW investigates climate-adaptive greenhouses and controlled cultivation of fresh, nutritious plant-based food near population centres. The local environment is part of the design.

GROW is a research project in development, not an operational greenhouse business, agricultural or energy network, active food producer, proven technology or government programme. No pilot, location, greenhouse size, crop selection, partner or customer has been established. The image is conceptual; it shows no existing GROW installation. Conviction is not yet evidence.
01 / Project model
The aim
How do we produce fresh food near cities by making the local environment part of the design?
Food production that fits the place.

GROW investigates whether fresh fruit, vegetables and other suitable plant-based food can be reliably produced near population centres in different climates. Not every location or crop has to prove suitable. Reliability, nutritional value, affordability and environmental consequences must be assessed together.
Working hypothesis / still to be tested

The proximity hypothesis: shorter distances could reduce transport time, spoilage and time between harvest and use. This has not been demonstrated. Local cultivation is not automatically cheaper or greener; imports from an efficient growing region may remain better. GROW does not have to win every comparison.
02 / Project model
The principle

Not the same greenhouse everywhere. A greenhouse that fits the place. Use the climate; don't blindly fight it. The aim can remain the same while greenhouse form, ventilation, cooling, heating, energy supply, water management and crops differ fundamentally.
Environment as input
Temperature, sunlight, wind, humidity, rain and seasons are the starting point. Where relevant, soil and environmental conditions belong in the investigation.
Local manufacturability
Water, energy, materials, skills and maintenance help determine feasibility. The choice must also fit crops, population centres and existing infrastructure.
Independently testable
GROW investigates production and preparation for distribution. It could connect to ordinary supermarkets and existing food systems; LOOP or HIVE are not prerequisites.
03 / Project model
Climate as a building material
Sun, wind, temperature, humidity and seasons are design inputs, not just obstacles. Local conditions must first be described, including extremes and proximity to people and infrastructure.
Still to be investigated. No universal greenhouse layout or location has been chosen. Conditions supporting a system elsewhere may be a constraint here.
04 / Project model
Hot and dry
In a hot, dry scenario, GROW could investigate how shading, airflow, heat-resistant design and suitable crops work together. This is a research direction, not a solved desert farming system.

Evaporative cooling requires responsible assessment of water and environmental effects. Rain harvesting or desalination is a research possibility only where location and economics justify it. Heat does not automatically mean greater water use: consumption and efficiency must be measured against an appropriate cultivation comparison. Potential savings from controlled cultivation are not an established GROW result either.
05 / Project model
Cold and dark

A northern scenario may require another system: retain heat, understand shorter growing seasons and choose crops that fit the energy economics. A warm-climate greenhouse is not copied unchanged into a cold region.
Artificial light is an option only when the comparison justifies it. Heating, lighting, structure and crop selection must be calculated together; reliability and affordability are not yet proven.
06 / Project model
Energy

Which energy system makes food production here reliable, affordable and environmentally defensible? The ambition is to use as much locally appropriate renewable energy as practical, without deciding the answer in advance.

Sun and wind do not guarantee continuous operation. Generation profiles, peak demand, storage, backup supplies and grid connections must be investigated. Renewable contribution and overall system performance have yet to be measured.
07 / Project model
Water
Water is a firm design requirement. GROW must investigate its source, use and consequences for the local environment. Recirculation is a mechanism to test, not a promised saving.

The comparison must include losses and treatment. Some locations or crops could prove unsuitable even if a greenhouse is technically possible. No yield automatically justifies an unsustainable water source.
08 / Project model
What do we grow?
No final crop list. Not every fruit or vegetable belongs everywhere. Selection must follow local needs and a transparent comparison of the entire production setup.
Imports may be more rational for a particular crop. Maximum biomass is not the same as usable nutritious production. A limited crop selection follows only from research.
09 / Project model
What must GROW demonstrate?
These are open questions, not answers. The model must be compared with existing local agriculture and imported food, with explicit boundaries for costs and environmental effects.
Can the system reliably produce usable quantities?
What does production cost per kilogram of usable food?
How much energy does the full system require?
How much water does it require, including losses and treatment?
How does it perform against conventional local cultivation?
How does it perform against imported food?
Does proximity actually reduce waste or logistics costs?
Can producers remain economically viable?
Which crops fit these conditions?
Which climates and locations are suitable, and which are not?
10 / Project model
First prototype

Start with one climate scenario and one location context. Investigate a small controlled greenhouse with a limited crop selection still to be chosen. Measure energy, water, usable yield and total costs; compare with real alternatives. This trial has not started.
Possible test / not started yet
Climate and location
Still to be determined; no land or region chosen
Greenhouse and dimensions
Still to be designed from the baseline
Crops
Still to be investigated and selected
Energy and water
System choice and measurement method still to be determined
Costs, partners and scheduling
Still to be calculated and determined
Before a prototype

No location, budget, dimensions, cultivation results, partners or data have been established. First investigate which test could teach us something; only then design and decide whether building is responsible.
11 / Project model
What do we measure?
Measurement boundaries, period, food quality and comparison basis must be established in advance. All outcomes below remain unknown.
Yield
How much usable food is produced, how consistent is it and how much crop is lost?Yet to be measured
How much usable food is produced, how consistent is it and how much crop is lost?
Water
How many litres per kilogram or another transparent unit are needed, including recirculation and losses?Yet to be measured
How many litres per kilogram or another transparent unit are needed, including recirculation and losses?
Energy
What is the energy per kilogram, renewable contribution, peak demand and need for storage or backup supplies?Yet to be measured
What is the energy per kilogram, renewable contribution, peak demand and need for storage or backup supplies?
Costs
What are the investment, operating costs and costs per unit of usable food?Yet to be measured
What are the investment, operating costs and costs per unit of usable food?
Logistics
What do distance to consumers, storage and spoilage require compared with existing supply routes?Yet to be measured
What do distance to consumers, storage and spoilage require compared with existing supply routes?
Nutrition
What usable nutritional value does the system deliver beyond total biomass alone?Yet to be measured
What usable nutritional value does the system deliver beyond total biomass alone?
12 / Project model
What could go wrong?
Conviction is not yet evidence. If GROW offers no meaningful improvement somewhere, we won't build GROW there. These objections remain open.
Challenge GROW.
What are we missing?
13 / Project model
Results
No results yet.
GROW has demonstrated no greenhouse, pilot, food production or measured saving. Actual outcomes, comparisons and limitations belong here later — including when the hypothesis fails.
14 / Project model
First understand the environment.

Define the first climate and location scenario and establish a transparent baseline: what is eaten here today, where does it come from and what does it cost in water, energy, transport and money? Only then determine whether GROW could improve something meaningful.

GROW investigates production and preparation for distribution. LOOP investigates distribution and access; HIVE investigates complete living environments. GROW could serve existing cities, shops and food chains. A future greenhouse could be near HIVE, but none of these projects requires another. No integrated system or supply arrangement has been agreed.
Access
Investigates the step from producer to existing communities.
Living environment
A possible nearby application, not a necessary customer.
Proposal
An affordability question; local production is not the predetermined answer.

title: HIVE — A complete living environment, built from the foundations. — BOUW
headings: From living concept to testable Cell.
content: BOUW PROJECT / LIVING ENVIRONMENT
Status — In development
HIVE
A complete living environment, built from the foundations.
Housing, food, primary care and everyday amenities as one system. The underlying foundation is what we repeat; implementation must fit the place and its people.

HIVE is a design and research project in development. It is not a construction company, property developer, housing provider, municipality, government programme or investment product. There is no operational neighbourhood or completed architectural plan. No homes have been built; there are no residents, pilots, land, partners, investors or demonstrated savings.
01 / Project model
The aim
How do we build affordable places to live that could be repeated almost anywhere in the world — with housing, food, primary care and everyday amenities nearby?
The same foundation. Local implementation.

HIVE investigates a complete living environment, not just a home. A new housing option. No prescribed way of life. Residents must choose for themselves whether it fits them. The hypothesis is that the physical foundations of daily life could be designed better together than added separately afterwards. Affordability, comfort, access and maintenance must be tested together.
Working hypothesis / still to be tested

This is a design hypothesis, not a proven chain or settled urban plan. A shared system structure does not mean neighbourhoods in the Netherlands, Zimbabwe or Poland must look the same. Climate, culture, materials, density, rules, economics and existing infrastructure require local choices.
02 / Project model
The HIVE Cell

The HIVE Cell is the smallest potentially repeatable, complete unit. The functions below are design and research requirements: we still need to discover what belongs within one Cell, what Cells could share and what must connect to existing systems. No final Cell, dimensions or capacity has been established.
Housing
Complete living spaces investigated for comfort, maintenance, quality and affordability. A low construction price alone is not enough.
Food
Access through a supermarket, food point or possible LOOP point. This function belongs in the design from the start, without assuming an existing operator or supply.
Primary care
Access to general practice or a primary care post, appropriately connected to pharmacies, emergency care, hospitals and existing healthcare systems. Capacity and organisation remain open.
Movement & community
Public and shared space, places to be active and safe walking routes. Where people like to gather and how accessible the space is must be investigated locally.
Water & energy
Water, electricity and other suitable energy supplies, sanitation and waste management must be designed to function and remain maintainable. Required capacity and costs remain unknown.
Connections
Digital connections, transport and access to work belong to a complete foundation. The design must not assume accessible jobs or infrastructure will emerge by themselves.
03 / Project model
Housing

The construction method remains open. Modular construction, prefabrication, compact apartments, small complete homes, local production, efficient traditional construction or another suitable system could be investigated. Containers, camper vans or a single technology are not chosen as the answer in advance.
Cheap construction with poor living conditions is not success. Finding the strongest local combination requires a fair comparison of full construction and use costs, quality and consequences.
04 / Project model
Everyday amenities
How much of daily life could take place close to home?

HIVE wants to design for human time and accessibility, not just maximum housing density. Food, primary care, movement, public space and daily needs should require fewer unnecessary journeys. Whether this works must be measured later; we promise no fixed walking distance or travel time.
Food from the start

A supermarket, food point or possible LOOP point could be part of the design. HIVE builds the living environment. LOOP investigates how nutritious food could become accessible there. LOOP currently operates no supermarket or distribution network.
Primary care nearby

A general practice or primary care post could be shared by an appropriate group of residents or Cells. Staffing, funding, capacity and connections to pharmacies, emergency care and hospitals must be investigated. No numbers of care providers or service areas have been established.
Accessible daily life

Safe routes, public space, movement, water, energy, sanitation, waste management and digital connections must be usable by diverse residents. Transport to work and amenities outside the Cell is also part of the system.
05 / Project model
The same foundation. Local implementation.

HIVE does not export a fixed Dutch neighbourhood design. It investigates whether one living system can be intelligently adapted to different places. What fits one region may be unsuitable or too expensive elsewhere.

These factors must be investigated alongside local conditions and possible residents' wishes. No location or local implementation has been chosen; comparability does not require identical architecture.
06 / Project model
Cell → Block → District → City
Demonstrate the smallest complete unit first. Then repeat what works.

A Cell that works as a model does not prove a whole city works. Every increase in scale requires renewed investigation of amenities, infrastructure, management, costs and quality of life. The names indicate a research direction, not fixed numbers of homes or residents.
Cell
Could the necessary functions together form a complete local foundation?
Block
What could be repeated and what must several Cells share?
District
Would care, transport, work connections and management continue to function as the system grows?
City
Is further repetition responsible, or does greater scale require a different model?
No step in scale is proven. Repetition is a possibility after testing; adjusting or stopping remains a valid outcome at every stage.
07 / Project model
What must HIVE demonstrate?
These questions remain unanswered. HIVE must investigate the entire living environment, including ownership, land, infrastructure and management, before calling it an affordable or repeatable model.
Could a complete home actually become substantially more affordable?
What does one complete living space cost to build?
What does maintenance cost during use?
What infrastructure must be ready before residents arrive?
Which amenities belong within a Cell and which between Cells?
Could local materials and labour reduce costs without losing quality?
Could the system adapt to different climates?
Would daily needs actually become easier to reach?
What happens when land is expensive?
Who owns the land and who owns the homes?
Would renting, ownership, cooperative housing or another model fit?
How would infrastructure be funded?
Could repetition reduce construction and infrastructure costs?
Could repetition avoid monotonous neighbourhoods?
Would the model still work as it grows?
08 / Project model
First prototype

The research must first discover what trial is useful. The first test need not be a whole neighbourhood: a spatial model, cost model, construction prototype, individual living unit, infrastructure simulation or smaller test may fit better. No physical trial, location, country or budget has been established.
Possible test / not started yet
Test format
Still to be determined from the research question
Local context
Still to be determined; no country, city or plot chosen
Construction method
Still to be investigated and compared
Costs and infrastructure
Still to be calculated and modelled
Participation and scheduling
Still to be determined; no residents, partners or trial dates
Before a prototype

This is the development sequence, not a running programme. Testable requirements and an appropriate local context come before assumptions about land, construction or scale. Safety, accessibility, rights and maintenance must be considered from the design stage.
09 / Project model
What do we measure?

Each measure needs defined boundaries, method, comparison basis and limitations. This is a future measurement framework; no construction costs, housing expenses or accessibility have been demonstrated.
Home construction costs
What does a complete living space cost to build and maintain?Yet to be measured
What does a complete living space cost to build and maintain?
Housing expenses
What does living here actually cost the resident, including necessary amenities?Yet to be measured
What does living here actually cost the resident, including necessary amenities?
Accessibility
How much time and distance do food, primary care, public space and transport require for diverse residents?Yet to be measured
How much time and distance do food, primary care, public space and transport require for diverse residents?
Construction time
How long do construction and expansion actually take, including preparation and infrastructure?Yet to be measured
How long do construction and expansion actually take, including preparation and infrastructure?
Local production
What could realistically be made and built locally, under what conditions?Yet to be measured
What could realistically be made and built locally, under what conditions?
Maintenance
What is required to keep homes, amenities and infrastructure functioning?Yet to be measured
What is required to keep homes, amenities and infrastructure functioning?
Space
How much land and infrastructure does a complete living environment require?Yet to be measured
How much land and infrastructure does a complete living environment require?
Quality of life
Does affordability produce a place where people actually want to live?Yet to be measured
Does affordability produce a place where people actually want to live?
10 / Project model
What could go wrong?
A plan gets better through criticism, not by avoiding it. These possible failures deserve investigation before a beautiful drawing brushes them away.
Challenge HIVE.
What are we missing?
11 / Project model
Results
No results yet.

HIVE has built no homes, housed no residents and run no pilot. There are no land holdings, construction partners, government agreements or proven savings. When real tests take place, their measured outcomes and limitations belong here — including when the model disappoints.
12 / Project model
From living concept to testable Cell.

First define what a complete foundation must offer, investigate local implementation and model costs and infrastructure. Only then choose which small test would teach the most. Don't immediately draw a city or assume land, residents and construction.

HIVE investigates the living environment. LOOP investigates food accessibility and distribution. GROW could later explore a possible production layer near or serving population centres. They are separate research projects; their connection is a possibility, not an existing integrated system.
Physical foundation
The complete living environment as a design and research question.
Food accessibility
A separate project, not a distribution partner yet.
Possible production
A future production concept, not an operational supplier.

title: RISE — From goal to next step. — BOUW
headings: First demonstrate that the conversation helps.
content: BOUW PROJECT / PERSONAL PROGRESS
Status — In development
RISE
Everyone has a next step. RISE helps find it.
RISE investigates a personal AI guide that begins by listening. From understanding where you are to a meaningful goal, a realistic plan and a next step — with room to adjust along the way.

RISE is a research project in development. It is not a working support service, financial institution, lender, benefits system, subsidy programme or autonomous funding AI. There are no users, pilots, payments or proven outcomes. The image is conceptual and shows no existing RISE service. Conviction is not yet evidence.
01 / Project model
The aim
Could a conversation help someone find a better next step — and actually take it?
From goal to next step.

Your goal. Your choices. RISE helps with the next step. RISE wants to investigate whether long-term personal guidance helps people move from their current situation towards a goal they choose themselves. This could concern debt, study, work, craftsmanship, enterprise or a personal goal. Financially stable people may also need direction. Not solving someone's entire life in one conversation, but finding the next useful step together.
Working hypothesis / still to be tested
This is a hypothesis, not demonstrated effectiveness. Each person decides what progress means. RISE must not promise wellbeing, success or funding.
02 / Project model
The conversation

Begin with what someone says, not a form or predetermined pathway. For example: 'I want to get out of debt.' 'I want to become an electrician.' 'I want to start a business.' 'I want to study again.' Or: 'I don't know exactly what I want, but I can't go on like this.' These are illustrative examples, not statements from existing RISE users.
Listen
Explore what someone means, which circumstances matter and where uncertainty lies. Ask questions without shaming, manipulating or imposing a goal.
Understand
The person checks whether RISE understood correctly. A vague wish can become more concrete; not everything needs to be known or resolved immediately.
Keep talking
Remember relevant context only with consent, discuss agreed progress and reconsider when circumstances or goals change. How to do this safely and reliably still needs investigation.
03 / Project model
From goal to next step

TALK → UNDERSTAND → GOAL → PLAN → NEXT STEP → PROGRESS → ADJUST → CONTINUE. A plan is not a final answer: the conversation continues over time, with consent and room to stop or choose another direction.
RISE could help prepare practical tasks, explain recommendations and follow jointly agreed steps. This model has not been built or tested yet; context memory must not become a hidden dossier.
04 / Project model
What could RISE help build?

The routes are examples, not fixed programmes. For debt, RISE could help organise income and obligations, recognise urgency, prepare a feasible budget and find suitable debt support. It does not automatically pay off debt. For someone wanting to become an electrician, it could help investigate training, admission, applications, practical pathways, costs, tools, certification and transport — with checks by appropriate experts.

An illustrative example: 'I want to start a landscaping business.' First investigate the idea, assumptions, a simple plan, an initial customer test, costs, legal and administrative requirements, evidence and next step. Not immediately provide start-up capital. None of these examples is an existing pathway or result.
05 / Project model
When money does help

Could money be used more intelligently if we first understand what someone could change with it? Begin not with how much money someone wants, but with the concrete obstacle preventing the next step. Don't just give people resources. Help them build what they want to achieve with them.

Necessary tools, training, certification, transport, childcare, debt restructuring or limited start-up capital could be a bottleneck. This must be investigated case by case. RISE could help substantiate a need and propose a possible intervention; it does not allocate money independently or decide who 'deserves' it. No fund, funding source or allocation policy has been established.
06 / Project model
When money doesn't help

Capital is not always the answer. Information, an application, planning, time, guidance or professional help could fit better. The right financial intervention could also be zero: a design possibility, not a measured saving.
An ambition alone does not justify a payment. First test what actually blocks the step. Support must increase independence, not create dependence on RISE or funding.
07 / Project model
Human + AI

AI helps understand, plan and prepare; the person retains control. RISE must acknowledge uncertainty, explain recommendations and transfer to human or professional help when needed. It does not diagnose or replace necessary legal, financial or medical expertise.

Privacy is a design requirement: what data is actually needed, what can stay on the device, what must be stored and for how long? Can someone access, correct and delete data, and who has access? Which information must never influence funding decisions remains to be determined. Vulnerability in a conversation must not become a financial score. There will be no hidden worthiness score. Any consequential funding decisions require transparent criteria, understandable reasons, privacy and security, discrimination assessment, fraud protection, appropriate human oversight, reassessment and appeal, and clear limits on automation. These safeguards and their testing have not yet been developed or proven.
08 / Project model
What must RISE demonstrate?
The conversation hypothesis and any funding hypothesis require separate evidence. None of these questions has been answered yet.
Does long-term AI guidance actually improve achievement of self-chosen goals?
Do people continue using it meaningfully over time?
Are useful, feasible next steps found?
Does targeted financial support work better than untargeted support, if funding is responsibly tested later?
Are recommendations understandable and verifiable?
Can bias and unequal treatment be sufficiently limited?
Can users meaningfully challenge decisions and have them reassessed?
Can privacy and control actually be protected?
How do we prevent manipulation and fraud without unnecessary surveillance?
Does independence grow or dependence develop?
When must AI hand over to a person or expert?
09 / Project model
First prototype

The first test concerns guidance only: conversation → goal → next step → follow-up → adjustment. First investigate whether this produces useful progress before giving RISE any role in allocating money. No automated funding in the first trial.
Possible test / not started yet
Conversation model
Still to be designed and tested for boundaries
Context and consent
Still to be determined; minimal data as the starting point
Test group, duration and location
Still to be determined; no participants or pilot
Human support
Handover and oversight still to be developed
Budget and measurement plan
Still to be calculated and established
Funding
Not part of the first guidance trial
Before a prototype

This is a future trial framework. There is no working conversation partner, submission function, data storage or money allocation on this page. Funding research could be considered only later, with its own criteria and safeguards.
10 / Project model
What do we measure?

The person must influence what progress means. Measurement methods, consent, comparison basis and boundaries must be established beforehand. Measurability must not become an obligation to pursue an imposed goal.
Progress
Which jointly agreed steps are taken, and does someone move closer to their own goal?Yet to be measured
Which jointly agreed steps are taken, and does someone move closer to their own goal?
Usability
Are recommendations practical, and does the person understand the trade-offs?Yet to be measured
Are recommendations practical, and does the person understand the trade-offs?
Continuity
Is relevant context remembered and reused correctly with consent?Yet to be measured
Is relevant context remembered and reused correctly with consent?
Independence
Does someone become better able to move forward independently?Yet to be measured
Does someone become better able to move forward independently?
Safety
Do harmful recommendations, unwarranted certainty or errors in handover to human help occur?Yet to be measured
Do harmful recommendations, unwarranted certainty or errors in handover to human help occur?
Fairness
What differences emerge between relevant groups, and do appeal and reassessment work meaningfully?Yet to be measured
What differences emerge between relevant groups, and do appeal and reassessment work meaningfully?
Impact per intervention
Only if funding is tested later: what actually changed through the specific support, compared with an appropriate baseline?Yet to be measured
Only if funding is tested later: what actually changed through the specific support, compared with an appropriate baseline?
11 / Project model
What could go wrong?
These risks are real design questions, not objections we can dismiss in advance. A plan gets better through criticism, not by avoiding it.
Challenge RISE.
What are we missing?
12 / Project model
Results
No results yet.

There are no RISE users, pilots, funding outcomes, debt results, realised businesses or jobs, measured AI accuracy or proven interventions. Real measurements and limitations belong here later — even if guidance does not help.
13 / Project model
First demonstrate that the conversation helps.
Could a conversation help someone find a better next step — and actually take it? Begin by guiding and following up that step, with consent, privacy and human support built into the design.

Funding does not follow automatically. Test the guidance loop first; only then investigate whether a targeted intervention adds value and could be responsibly assessed. Money is a possible tool, not the product.
Position
A direction towards greater independence, not a proven RISE effect.
Position
A possible goal direction; training and requirements must be investigated case by case.
Position
Debt remains one possible route, not RISE's entire mission.

title: MEND — Working with the body's repair processes. — BOUW
content: BOUW PROJECT / BIOLOGY & REPAIR
Status — In development
MEND
Could we better help the body heal itself?
MEND investigates how biomaterials, biological structures and the environment of tissue repair could work with repair processes the body already possesses.

MEND is an experimental research concept, not a biotech company, healthcare provider, treatment, medical device, operational laboratory or proven regenerative technology. MEND has no experiments, patients, trials, partners, patents or breakthroughs. The image is conceptual, not an existing MEND laboratory. Conviction is not yet evidence.
01 / Project model
The aim
How could materials, environment and biology work with repair processes the body already possesses?
The body is doing the biological work.

MEND wants to investigate whether we could better understand, support or provide structure for existing repair processes. Tissue repair, wound healing, biomaterials, tissue-material interaction and regenerative medicine form a research direction, not a platform that regenerates the human body.
Working hypothesis / still to be tested

MEND hypothesis: a carefully designed material and environment could support repair processes under certain conditions. What, where and how must first be scientifically defined. Any future use must be voluntary and respect bodily autonomy; MEND proposes no compulsory treatment. No faster or scar-free healing, organ regeneration, successful integration or treatment has been demonstrated.
02 / Project model
The body already builds

Established biology, not a MEND discovery: humans have repair processes, but limited regenerative capacity. Wound repair can involve scarring; it does not mean every tissue fully returns to its original state. MEND begins by studying these processes.
What biology already shows

The body renews cells and can repair tissue damage. During wound repair, cells and the extracellular matrix — the structure around cells — change together. This is general biological knowledge, not evidence for a MEND intervention.
What MEND assumes
A material might provide a useful environment or temporary structure. That is a hypothesis, not a discovery or treatment.
What MEND must test
First determine a specific material question, suitable experimental model and measurable criteria. Model results must not be presented directly as effectiveness in humans.
03 / Project model
Material meets body

Which properties could make a material or scaffold — a supporting structure — suitable for contact with tissue? MEND must investigate structure, properties and biological responses together, without assuming suitability.
Research questions, not a solved design. A material could seem technically useful yet cause unwanted responses. No MEND material has been selected, characterised or proven safe.
04 / Project model
A temporary structure

Could a carefully designed temporary structure provide an environment in which a person's own cells organise and repair or replace damaged tissue? This is the scaffold hypothesis MEND wants to define, not a claimed therapy.

A structure does not work independently as a substitute for biology. Whether cells respond appropriately, whether degradation proceeds responsibly and whether any support occurs are unanswered questions. No experiments on humans proposed.
05 / Project model
The repair environment

Repair requires more than one material or nutrient. The research question must account for the biological and mechanical environment. The body does the healing; nutrients are resources and conditions supporting processes, not a standalone healing solution.

These are factors for literature review and model selection, not diagnosis or treatment advice. MEND has no effective dose, material combination or repair protocol. Which factors are relevant and measurable depends on the chosen question.
06 / Project model
From hypothesis to experiment

QUESTION → HYPOTHESIS → MODEL → EXPERIMENT → MEASURE → CRITICISM → REPEAT. First describe established knowledge, what is merely assumed and which observation would support or refute the hypothesis. Medical expectations must not outrun evidence.

Before a trial: define measurement criteria, controls, reproducibility, safety boundaries and model limitations. Sources must substantiate general knowledge; they are not MEND results. NIGMS describes limited human regeneration and the extracellular matrix in wound repair. A literature review for the specific MEND question has not yet been performed.
07 / Project model
First prototype

Begin with literature review and material requirements. Design or computational models could help where appropriate. Any safe laboratory characterisation and in vitro studies come only later, with qualified scientific supervision, suitable facilities and applicable review. No human research as the first step.
Possible test / not started yet
First question
Still to be scientifically defined
Material and model
Still to be determined; no design or experiment established
Facilities and supervision
Still to be determined; no active laboratory or partners
Safety and measurement criteria
Still to be developed before any trial
Costs and scheduling
Still to be calculated and determined
Before a prototype
This is a possible research framework, not a running trial. In vitro findings would describe only the chosen model, not prove clinical effectiveness or safety.
08 / Project model
What do we measure?
Every measure must fit the eventual research question and actual model. No MEND material, biological or repair outcomes exist yet.
Material

title: CLARKE — The last lift we ever need to build. — BOUW
headings: First determine what would have to be true.
content: SPACE INFRASTRUCTURE
Status — Extremely early
CLARKE
The last lift we ever need to build.
CLARKE investigates what a permanent connection between Earth and space would require technically, economically and socially. Not as a promise, but as research over an extremely long horizon.

CLARKE is a theoretical research direction, not an active engineering programme, funded project, construction site or space organisation. Feasibility with materials demonstrated today has not been established. No implementation, location, prototype or result is promised. The image is a concept, not an engineering drawing. The headline expresses ambition, not a prediction.
01 / Project model
The idea
What would a permanent physical transport connection between Earth and space require?
A connection, not a promise to launch.

The classic Earth-based space elevator concept investigates a long, tensioned tether from Earth's surface to beyond geostationary orbit, with climbers travelling along it. This is a theoretical infrastructure concept, not a tower simply built ever higher. A described theory is not yet an implementable system.
Working hypothesis / still to be tested

The name refers to Arthur C. Clarke and the idea's history in science fiction and engineering. The reference is inspiration, not technical substantiation. CLARKE has no dimensions, travel times, load capacities or material breakthroughs.
02 / Project model
Why a lift at all?

Could permanent infrastructure change the economics, repeatability and accessibility of transport beyond Earth's surface? The comparison must include future launch technology. Cheaper or cleaner is a question, not a quality CLARKE already possesses.
Repeatability
Could climbers operate reliably along a permanent connection, and what would that require in energy, inspection and replacement?
Accessibility
Who would gain access and under what conditions? Infrastructure must not automatically mean exclusive control by one government, company or movement.
A fair comparison
Construction, operations, safety and environmental consequences must be compared with launch alternatives. A permanent system is not automatically better.
03 / Project model
The problem

The engineering difficulty is fundamental. A working subsystem would not prove the full connection. Materials, orbital mechanics, dynamics, environment and management must be investigated as an integrated system.
These are research areas, not a solved design. CLARKE has no anchor location, power supply, construction programme or safety plan.
04 / Project model
The materials problem

The tether requires an exceptional strength-to-weight ratio. Material behaviour must remain viable across great lengths, including joints, defects, environmental loads and maintenance. Material capability is a central unresolved prerequisite.
A favourable property of a material sample does not solve the whole practical problem. CLARKE claims no existing material that makes a complete Earth-based space elevator possible.
05 / Project model
What must CLARKE demonstrate?
We distinguish theoretical descriptions from feasibility. CLARKE has answered none of these questions.
Could a suitable tether ever be manufactured at the required scale?
Could the system remain dynamically stable?
Could climbers function reliably?
Could energy be supplied efficiently and reliably?
Are space debris and environmental risks manageable?
Could failures be handled with acceptable safety?
Would it outperform future launch technology economically?
Who owns and governs infrastructure extending into space?
How do we protect access, international control and freedom against concentrated power?
06 / Project model
First prototype
Not tomorrow.

Meaningful first steps would be literature review, engineering models, materials research and small, defined subsystem questions. Not building a tower to space. First determine which assumption is testable and whether further research is justified.

Which assumption fails?

CLARKE has no engineering, material or prototype outcomes. If research cannot establish feasibility, that is a legitimate outcome. A theory is not a construction result.
10 / Project model
First determine what would have to be true.
Which assumptions must demonstrably hold before CLARKE deserves more than theoretical research? Begin with the decisive constraints, not a construction date.
No owner, exclusive access model or international governance structure has been chosen. BOUW's freedom test applies here too: does the system expand control and possibilities, or concentrate power?

title: BOUW Basics — Healthy food as a basic provision — BOUW
headings: Healthy food as a basic provision.
First make sure everyone can eat well.
A good idea must stand up to calculation.
What do we still need to demonstrate?
No promises. First prove it works.
content: BOUW PROPOSAL 01 — FOOD
Healthy food as a basic provision.
What if the Netherlands used public resources to make healthy staples more affordable — and ensured nobody had to go without a good foundation?
BOUW Basics
Under investigation
A proposal to investigate.No trial started yet.No measured results yet.
Show the idea.Show the system.Then show the math.
01 / The principle
First make sure everyone can eat well.

BOUW Basics is a proposal with two layers: public support makes a defined basket of nutritious staples more affordable according to household income. Alongside this, any household in the Netherlands could request a free basic basket. The basket does not replace a supermarket or provide everything someone eats; it offers a nutritional foundation from which people can prepare their own meals.
More affordable according to income
Healthy staples receive stronger support at lower household incomes. As income rises, support gradually decreases.
BOUW Basics basket
A basket of healthy staples that any household could request. No complicated assessment or proof that you're poor enough.

For the income-related layer, we still need to determine which income counts, how support tapers and how privacy is protected. The free basket has no income condition in this proposal. Product choice, quantities, allergies and individual nutritional needs still require investigation.
02 / The foundation
What's in the foundation?
No luxury basket. No complete diet. A healthy foundation.
Possible product categories. The composition is not yet fixed.
03 / The system
From production to household.

BOUW wants to investigate how local agriculture, greenhouse production, existing suppliers and efficient distribution could work together. No production method is predetermined. We compare costs, supply reliability, reach and losses before choosing an implementation.

No suppliers, locations or distribution partners have been established yet. The request process, personal data protection, food safety, freedom of choice and how support reduces prices also need development. No basket can be requested yet.
04 / Show the calculation
A good idea must stand up to calculation.
We publish the assumptions, calculations and limitations behind the proposal. If the numbers contradict the idea, the proposal changes.
Cost per person / week

Being calculated

Being calculated
No budget, defined basket or calculated nutritional value yet. Quantities, costs and capacity will be published here only with assumptions, sources and limitations.
05 / Start small
Start with 100 people.
Not the whole Netherlands immediately. Test one local system with 100 participants first. Measure costs, waste, nutritional value, use and logistics. Improve what doesn't work. Scale only what does.
100 participants is a proposed trial size, not an existing pilot. Later steps follow only if results justify them. Adjusting or stopping is also a possible outcome.
06 / Evidence
What do we still need to demonstrate?
What we already know

No verified research sources have been added to BOUW Basics yet. Effectiveness, nutritional suitability and economic feasibility have not been demonstrated. This is a proposal to investigate, not a proven solution.
What we still need to demonstrate

No results yet.

No pilot has started or been carried out yet. Measured outcomes with measurement method, costs, sources and limitations belong here later. Disappointing results will also be published. The growth path is conditional, not a commitment to nationwide implementation.
From proposal to evidence
