title: Fresh food should cost less — BOUW
headings: Where does the price of fresh food come from?
Lower costs, from producer to consumer.
Start small. Then measure. Then decide.
A good plan must withstand criticism.
content: Affordable living
PLAN TO BUILD / 02
Fresh food should cost less
Why is fresh, healthy food often more expensive than highly processed food — and how much of that could we actually change?

Healthy eating should not be the luxury option. BOUW investigates whether local production, intelligent greenhouses and shorter food chains could make fresh, nutritious food structurally more affordable for everyone. The price comparison itself must also be investigated: by product, season and comparable quantity. This is a working idea, not a proven solution or promised price reduction.
From question to testable plan
01 / The problem
Where does the price of fresh food come from?

The central question is which costs arise between production and purchase, and which could actually be reduced. We want to compare fresh products and alternatives carefully, without assuming fresh food is always more expensive or one production method is advantageous everywhere.

Energy, labour, land, construction, finance, packaging, transport, storage, waste and distribution could be parts of that bill. Which items are decisive may vary by crop and region. Their share of the final consumer price has not yet been substantiated in this plan.

This proposal concerns affordability for everyone. 'Healthy food as a foundation' asks another question: should young people have access to a nutritional foundation even when lower prices are not enough for their household? A more efficient chain and guaranteed access are different investigations.
02 / The proposal
Lower costs, from producer to consumer.

The working idea is to compare different ways of producing and distributing. We investigate whether unnecessary costs could disappear without losing sight of quality, nutritional value, reliability or viable producer compensation.
Possible mechanisms · hypotheses to investigate

Still to be investigated: whether these mechanisms actually reduce costs, for which crops and under what conditions. More production or fewer intermediaries does not automatically mean a lower retail price; capacity, demand, market power and the distribution of savings must be investigated.
Closer is a possibility, not a guarantee.

Systems like LOOP and GROW could play a role in local or regional production. This is a possibility to investigate, not existing supply or collaboration. Energy and construction costs could change the assessment. Imports could be more efficient in some circumstances; local production must be compared with real alternatives, not chosen as the winner in advance.
Possible implementation
Which chain could we test?
Possible implementation
Still to be investigated

No production method, crop, location or distribution format has been chosen. We must establish who invests, who bears risk, who receives any savings and how lower costs could appear in consumer prices. Supply reliability, quality and consequences for producers also need investigation.
03 / Start with a pilot
Start small. Then measure. Then decide.

Start small. Then measure. Then decide. No pilot has started yet. A possible trial would compare one or a few products and a defined chain with a clearly described existing situation. We must determine in advance how to make seasons, quality, quantities and any subsidies comparable, and when to adjust or stop the approach.

Still to be determined

Still to be designed; no buyers or partners established

What we already know

No verified research sources have been added to this plan yet. We therefore present no proven price advantage from local greenhouses, shorter chains or greater production. Affordable fresh food is our ambition; effectiveness and economic feasibility still need substantiation.
What we still need to demonstrate

These are open questions, not objections with ready answers. They must be part of the research and the decision whether to test.
06 / Results
No results yet.

No pilot has been carried out yet. Measured costs, consumer prices and other outcomes with measurement method, comparison basis, sources and limitations belong here later. A more expensive approach or savings that fail to reach households must also be visible. There are currently no demonstrated price reductions or savings.
07 / Next step
From idea to pilot.

First make the comparison precise. Only when products, alternatives and full costs are well defined can we assess which hypothesis deserves a small trial. The outcome may also be that local production offers no advantage in a particular situation.

title: Move every day — BOUW
headings: A daily foundation, with room for difference.
Start small. Then measure. Then decide.
A good plan must withstand criticism.
content: Growing up healthy
PLAN TO BUILD / 03
Move every day
What if movement were as natural a part of young people's lives as education?

BOUW wants to investigate how young people could have a strong daily foundation of movement, sport and practical development. The aim is healthier, fitter and more self-reliant young people — not punishment, appearance or sporting performance. This is a proposal under investigation. Whether participation would be voluntary, encouraged or compulsory also remains open.
From question to testable plan
01 / The problem
Is movement accessible to everyone?

Do young people have enough opportunities to move regularly? Do their environment, daily schedules and available amenities make that possible for everyone? BOUW first wants to understand possible barriers, without assuming all young people have the same problem.

Costs, travel time, safety, accessibility and alignment with someone's interests can raise questions. Disability, chronic illness, mental strain or earlier negative sporting experiences also deserve attention. Which factors actually form barriers and for whom must be investigated.

We have not yet added verified sources about the scale of the issue to this plan. We therefore make no statement about how many young people move too little or the effect of a programme not yet designed.
02 / The proposal
A daily foundation, with room for difference.

The working idea is a daily movement framework with different activities and appropriate guidance. No uniform performance requirement or single exercise programme for everyone, but room for age, interests, abilities, recovery and personal circumstances.
Possible activities · programme still to be investigated

Still to be investigated: duration, intensity, frequency, guidance, safety and individual adaptations. This list is not training advice. No fixed performance standards or extreme requirements have been established.
Health as the goal. Room for the individual.

Personal freedom and physical and mental health must be part of the design. Young people differ: the same offering may be accessible to one and unsuitable for another. We must investigate which roles young people, parents, schools and local providers can and want to take, without fixing their responsibilities or available time in advance.
Voluntary, encouraged or compulsory?

Possible compulsory sport is an open design question, not decided BOUW policy. First establish whether a daily movement foundation is desirable and feasible, and whether support could achieve the same aim better than coercion. The following considerations are research questions, not proven effects.
Voluntary
How do we preserve choice while reaching young people who currently find participation difficult? What could an accessible, attractive offering without obligation achieve?
Encouraged
Could guidance, affordable provision and appropriate incentives support participation? How do we prevent rewards creating pressure or widening differences between young people?
Compulsory

Can a minimum movement expectation be justified? Who decides what is appropriate, which exceptions apply and what happens if someone doesn't participate? How do we prevent enforcement or punishment undermining the aim?

No option has been chosen. The freedom test must be able to reject this idea of our own. Any obligation requires a much higher threshold: necessity → evidence → proportionality → alternatives → consequences for rights and freedom. An attractive voluntary offering is the starting point; coercion requires separate, strong justification. A voluntary pilot would not itself demonstrate the justification or effectiveness of coercion. We currently propose no sanctions or enforcement rules.
Possible implementation
How could it work?
Possible implementation
Still to be investigated

No implementation format or collaboration has been established. Parents', schools' and providers' roles, age boundaries, privacy, accessibility, oversight and necessary expertise remain open. There must also be room to object, opt out or find an appropriate alternative. Voluntary, encouraged and compulsory participation must be assessed separately.
03 / Start with a pilot
Start small. Then measure. Then decide.

Start small. Then measure. Then decide. No BOUW pilot has been carried out or started yet. A possible first trial should investigate whether safe, accessible, voluntary provision fits young people. Participation conditions, consent, guidance and stop criteria must be developed in advance. A trial is not nationwide implementation and does not automatically decide compulsory sport.
Hypothetical pilot framework · no trial started yet
Location
Still to be determined
Number of participants and ages
Still to be determined
Duration
Still to be determined
Movement programme
To be developed with appropriate expertise and young people's input
Participation and consent
Still to be determined; no obligation or sanctions established
Adaptations and safety
To be designed for diverse physical and mental abilities
Cost per participant
To be calculated
Possible measurements
Participation, persistence, wellbeing, fitness, injuries, enjoyment, dropout and costs — measurement methods still to be determined
Stop criteria and evaluation
To be determined in advance, including unwanted effects
04 / Costs
What resources would this require?
This is the structure for a cost model. Amounts, volumes and assumptions still need development; there is no budget yet.
05 / Evidence
Evidence before conviction.
What we already know

No verified research sources have been added to this plan yet. We therefore provide no scientific conclusions on health effects, participation or compulsion. Our starting point is that young people should have opportunities for appropriate movement. Whether this framework works and which form of participation is justified still needs substantiation.
What we still need to demonstrate
Criticism & risks
A good plan must withstand criticism.
These are open questions, not objections with ready answers. They must be part of the research and the decision whether to test.
06 / Results
No results yet.

No BOUW pilot has been carried out yet. Measured outcomes with methods, source references and limitations belong here later, including injuries, dropout and young people's experiences. Null results and harmful effects must also be visible. There are currently no results justifying this proposal or compulsory sport.
07 / Next step
From idea to pilot.

First determine what responsible research should test. Designing an accessible movement foundation and investigating compulsion are separate steps. Only after substantiation and evaluation can we decide whether the idea deserves to proceed.
Challenge this proposal
What are we missing?
A plan gets better through criticism, not by avoiding it.

title: Our vision — BOUW
headings: The Netherlands can do more than manage problems.We can build solutions.
A conviction is not yet an outcome.
Make the foundations more abundant and affordable. Then give people more room to build their own lives.
content: Our vision / No promises. Plans to build.
The Netherlands can do more than manage problems.We can build solutions.

BOUW chooses a country that develops ideas, acknowledges uncertainty and investigates what works in practice. Our convictions give us direction. Evidence must show which solutions actually bring us closer to it.
Not left against right.Not optimism against pessimism.Building over standing still.
Concept image / a possible future
Ambition with open eyes
A conviction is not yet an outcome.
We show what we believe, where we want to go and what still needs investigation.
Principles
What BOUW fundamentally believes. A conviction is not evidence of an effect.
Positions
The direction we want to take the Netherlands. No fully developed package of measures.
Proposals
Concrete mechanisms we still need to investigate, calculate and test.
Projects
Systems and concepts we could design, develop and test.
Results
What has actually been measured and demonstrated, with sources and limitations. No BOUW pilot results have been published on this site yet.
Principles / Four pillars
What we build on.
These are convictions about our chosen direction. How we put them into practice needs careful development and testing.
01 / Principle
Healthy people
A strong society begins with people who have the foundations to live well.
Daily meals or movement expectations are possible approaches. Their form and effectiveness are not yet established.
02 / Principle
A country that builds
The Netherlands needs renewed confidence to build what it needs.
Ambition requires feasible plans. Speed, affordability and liveability must be investigated together.
03 / Principle
More freedom through strong foundations
Freedom means more when the basics don't consume your whole life.

BOUW builds possibilities, not obligations. A good system gives people more choice over their own lives — not less. The freedom test investigates unnecessary coercion alongside effectiveness, costs and consequences.
04 / Principle
Try. Measure. Improve.
Government and society must become better at acknowledging uncertainty.
Failure is allowed. Hiding it isn't.
Assessing a plan
The freedom test
Does this give people more control over their own lives, or less?

A solution that works technically but needlessly takes away freedom is not yet a good plan. We assess evidence, feasibility, costs, risks, results and personal control — even when that rules out our own ideas.

Government and society have responsibilities for legislation, safety, infrastructure and shared services. The test asks whether a restriction is necessary and proportionate, and whether a freer alternative can achieve the same aim.
Positions / Our direction
What we want to change.
Twelve directions, with room for investigation. The goals set the course; their implementation is not settled policy.
The foundation for living well.
Position / Intended direction
Fresh, nutritious food should not be a luxury. BOUW wants to investigate how production, technology, shorter chains and greater supply could lower actual costs.
Implementation / Still to be investigated
Local production is not automatically cheaper. Investment, energy, import alternatives and the distribution of any savings must be considered.
Position / Intended direction
Young people's access to nutritious food should not depend entirely on household income. A guaranteed nutritional foundation deserves investigation, beginning with a testable pilot design.
Implementation / Still to be investigated
Composition, access, universal or targeted support, implementation and costs remain open questions. No BOUW pilot has started.
Position / Intended direction
We want more homes and more room for liveable neighbourhoods. Faster, more affordable construction methods, including modular models, must be developed and tested.
Implementation / Still to be investigated
We present no proven construction rate or cost saving. Quality, infrastructure and liveability belong in the testing.
Position / Intended direction
Sport and physical development deserve a much stronger place in growing up. The aim is health and possibilities, with room for differences between young people.
Implementation / Still to be investigated

The balance between encouragement, accessibility, expectations and compulsion still needs investigation. Compulsory sport is not established BOUW policy. The freedom test sets a higher standard: necessity, evidence, proportionality, alternatives and consequences for rights and freedom. This research could also reject compulsory participation.
A country that creates possibilities.
Position / Intended direction
Construction, technology, agriculture, manufacturing and other practical skills deserve respect as serious routes to a good future. We want learning to make things and craftsmanship to count fully.
Implementation / Still to be investigated
Which education and development pathways fit must be developed with attention to young people, educational quality and feasibility.
Position / Intended direction
Productive work, learning skills and entrepreneurship should provide a credible route to greater independence and a better life.
Implementation / Still to be investigated
This is a direction, not a promise about income or purchasing power. Concrete measures require cost estimates and investigation of their effects.
Position / Intended direction
Intervene earlier. BOUW wants to prevent manageable financial problems becoming lasting personal and social harm.
Implementation / Still to be investigated
How prevention, knowledge and guidance could work must be developed and tested. There are no results from a BOUW debt programme yet.
08 / Position
BOUW wants to investigate whether the Netherlands could become an important hub for nutritious plant-based products from Dutch and international farmers and growers.

The direction: connect strong, fair returns for farmers and growers with an abundant supply of fresh, nutritious products. We want to investigate whether that combination could make healthy food accessible to young people. Fair compensation, sufficient supply and low consumer prices do not automatically go together; the full model must be calculated.

One possible approach is access to a nutritious, fresh daytime meal for young people aged approximately 13–17, particularly during secondary education. That age group, meal concept, access and funding are proposals to investigate, not an established programme.

We also want to explore how nutrition, physical development, education and preparation for practical skilled work could reinforce each other. This requires carefully developed education and work-based learning pathways, not simply letting young people leave school.
Proposals / Still to be investigated

BOUW currently pays no farmers, imports no food and runs no meal programme. There are no agreements with schools. Economic feasibility, nutritional substantiation, responsibilities and implementation still need investigation.

A future pathway must fit existing compulsory education and, where applicable, qualification requirements, and undergo legal and educational development. This proposal does not mean a 13-year-old can leave school to work for BOUW.
Progress that stands up to testing.
Position / Intended direction

AI, automation, biotechnology and engineering should expand human possibilities, abundance and quality of life. We want to assess technology by what it delivers for people, beyond extra productivity alone.
Implementation / Still to be investigated
Possible applications require investigation of effectiveness, safety, freedom and consequences. A technical idea is not yet a proven improvement.
Position / Intended direction
Where practical, major new interventions should begin with measurable pilots. Define in advance what we want to learn, what it costs and when continuing, adjusting or stopping is justified.
Implementation / Still to be investigated
A small trial does not automatically prove nationwide implementation works. Scale, context and limitations must remain part of the assessment.
Position / Intended direction
Publish failures and negative results alongside successes. A failed experiment can teach us something; hiding it prevents fair assessment.
Implementation / Still to be investigated
This is our standard for future tests. We claim no already completed studies or published pilot results by saying this.
Position / Intended direction
Assess ideas by evidence, consequences, feasibility, freedom and results. Their traditional place on the political left or right should not determine whether we investigate them seriously.
Implementation / Still to be investigated
Constructive building also requires the ability to revise our own assumptions. An attractive idea must withstand criticism and testing.
Building over standing still
Make the foundations more abundant and affordable. Then give people more room to build their own lives.

No list of promises for four years from now. This is the direction BOUW wants to take the Netherlands — and the ideas we want to investigate to get there.

01—04 / Growing up well
A healthy foundation should be within reach.
01 / Position
Fresh food should cost less
Fresh, nutritious plant-based food should become much more affordable. Healthy eating should not be the luxury option.
Under investigation Possible approach

BOUW investigates whether increased supply from Dutch and international growers, greenhouse technology, efficient logistics, shorter chains where useful and less waste could lower actual costs. For households that still struggle to afford healthy food, we want to investigate whether support could vary with household income.
Local production is not automatically cheaper. Full costs, import alternatives and who receives any savings remain open questions. Income-related support is not an established system.
02 / Position
Good food for young people building their future
Young people should be able to learn, develop and work without going through the day hungry.
Under investigation Possible approach

We want to investigate access to fresh, nutritious meals for secondary-school-age young people and for young people in future recognised practical education and work pathways. Eligibility, suitable ages, funding and how meals would be offered remain open.
BOUW runs no meal programme and has no agreements with schools or training organisations. Any pathways need educational and legal development.
03 / Position
A personal food basket
Support for healthy eating should be simple, appropriate and accessible. A nutritional foundation need not mean the same basket for everyone.
Under investigation Possible approach

One possible approach is a simple government system through which eligible people could receive recurring baskets of fresh plant-based products. Conditions, composition, funding and implementation still need investigation.

We are investigating a concept for a new government service using DigiD through which someone could arrange access to a suitable basket. No service has been built, no DigiD integration exists and there is no government agreement. An accessible alternative for people unable to participate digitally must also be investigated.

Data minimisation is the starting point. We do not collect height, weight or health information simply because we can. Such data is sensitive; necessity, privacy, security, retention periods and an appropriate legal basis must first be carefully developed. This page requests or collects no personal data.
04 / Position
Movement belongs in growing up
Physical development and regular movement deserve a normal, strong place in growing up. The aim is health and possibilities, not punishment or uniform performance.
Under investigation Possible approach

Sport, walking, running, strength development, practical physical work and other accessible activities are possible elements. We also want to investigate whether structured physical development could fit future practical education and work pathways. Compulsory sport or a minimum participation expectation could be investigated, but is not established policy. The freedom test requires a much higher threshold: necessity, evidence, proportionality, alternatives and consequences for rights and freedom. Without strong justification, that option is ruled out.

Ordinary school absence does not automatically place a child in a BOUW programme. No programme or placement arrangement exists. Freedom of choice, appropriate guidance and legal and educational assessment must be developed first.
The Netherlands already functions.
So perhaps we should ask less about keeping the Netherlands running — and more about making it run better.
05 / Position
The Netherlands as a hub for plant-based food

BOUW wants to investigate whether the Netherlands could become an exceptional international hub for nutritious plant-based products. Strong, fair returns for growers should go together with wider access to good food here.
Under investigation Possible approach

We want to explore logistics, ports, agriculture, greenhouse expertise, food technology and international trade, alongside the possible role of Dutch and international farmers and growers. The question is how a large, reliable supply could make healthy eating simpler and more affordable, while preserving fair producer compensation.

This is a system to investigate, not simply more imports. BOUW has no grower agreements, import programmes or operational food infrastructure. LOOP and GROW are concepts, not evidence that this chain already exists.
06—10 / More room to live
Build what people need.
06 / Position
Heating should be affordable
Household heating should remain affordable. How it is provided must also be assessed for health, safety and environmental consequences.
Under investigation Possible approach

We want to investigate whether fireplaces, modern wood heating and responsibly sourced firewood could play a useful role for some households. Possible ideas include reducing or removing certain taxes on suitable equipment where public benefit is demonstrated, and better access to affordable, responsibly sourced wood. None of these measures is established.

This is no heating advice or proposal declaring wood heating suitable everywhere. Health risks and effects on neighbours belong in the research from the beginning. 'Tax-free fireplaces' is not BOUW policy.
07 / Position
Practical learning is real education
Anyone who thrives through building, repairing, growing, cooking, designing or making deserves a serious educational path to adulthood. Craftsmanship deserves real standing.
Under investigation Possible approach

We want to explore recognised pathways where education, craftsmanship, movement, good food and practical experience reinforce each other. The necessary guidance, quality requirements and responsibilities still need development.

A future pathway must fit existing compulsory education and, where applicable, qualification requirements. If education rules needed changing, that would require explicit legal and democratic development. This is no permission for 13-year-olds to leave school, and BOUW currently offers no recognised pathway.
08 / Position
Build until housing becomes normal again
We want to address housing shortages by building much more, with attention to affordability and liveable neighbourhoods.
Under investigation Possible approach

Modular construction, faster methods, alternative neighbourhood models, smaller affordable homes and new materials and production techniques deserve development and testing. Quality, infrastructure and full costs must be part of the assessment.
HIVE explores this as a housing concept. It is not operational and BOUW has no demonstrated construction rates, completed homes or savings.
09 / Position
Address debt before it takes over lives
Small financial problems should not needlessly grow into years of harm. Recovery should be possible.
Under investigation Possible approach

BOUW wants to intervene earlier, explore simpler routes out of problematic debt and investigate systems that support recovery. Knowledge and guidance are possible elements; effectiveness and costs must be tested.
RISE is a concept to develop, not an existing support service. There are no measured results from a BOUW debt programme.
10 / Position
Work should pay off again
Anyone learning useful skills, working and contributing should have a credible path to independence.
Under investigation Possible approach
We want to investigate how taxes, benefits, housing costs and other systems interact, so earning more could actually create room in someone's life. Effects must be considered case by case.
This is a research direction. This position contains no specific tax plan, calculated purchasing-power gain or established measure.
11—13 / Open eyes, better ideas
Progress must stand up to testing.
11 / Position
Technology should make people stronger
AI, automation, biotechnology, engineering and new production methods should expand human possibilities and abundance. Technology should deliver more than extra productivity alone.
Under investigation Possible approach

We want to assess applications for their effectiveness, consequences, safety and contribution to quality of life. Technical possibilities are a starting point for research, not a guarantee of social benefit.
GROW and MEND are concepts where such questions could be explored. Speculative applications, especially in health and biotechnology, are not proven technologies or treatments.
12 / Position
Try first. Then measure. Then scale.
Where practical, government and society should test ideas fairly before committing the whole country to them.
Under investigation Possible approach

A plan must state in advance what we want to learn, what success means, what it costs and when we adjust or stop. A pilot is a research step; a positive result in one context does not automatically justify nationwide implementation.
Problem → Plan → Pilot → Measure → Publish → Improve → Scale or stop
Publish setbacks, negative outcomes and limitations too. Our proposals have no BOUW pilot results yet; testable designs must first be developed.
Pilot needed A testable design is needed before a trial. No BOUW pilot is running yet.
13 / Position
Good ideas have no political colour
Don't begin with 'Is this left or right?' Begin with 'Does it work?'
Under investigation Possible approach

Assess an idea by evidence, consequences, feasibility, affordability, freedom and measurable results. We must be able to revise our own assumptions and let go of even a cherished idea when support is lacking.
No promises. Plans to build.
From direction to a testable plan.
Our convictions set the course. The next step is to investigate, calculate and honestly test what could actually work.

title: Participate — BOUW
headings: BOUW doesn't ask you to agree with us.
content: Building begins with a question
BOUW doesn't ask you to agree with us.
Help us find out what works.
A plan gets better through criticism, knowledge and evidence. You don't have to join anything to contribute.
Four ways to contribute.
Think with us
Does an assumption fail? Do you see an unintended consequence, a better alternative or something we are missing? Criticism moves a plan forward.
Build with us

Bring knowledge or practical experience: agriculture, food and logistics, construction, engineering, care and research, economics, education, AI and software, design, policy or law. We are exploring what's needed; there are no existing teams or programmes to join.
Share a source
Share evidence that supports an idea and evidence that contradicts it, exposes a risk or reveals an alternative. Explain what the source covers and what we can learn from it.
Help build a pilot

Help think through a small, measurable test: what question, approach and measurements would be useful? This is interest in future research, not enrolment in a running pilot. There are no published BOUW pilot results.
Your contribution
What are we missing?
Choose a subject and describe your idea, question, experience or source. This is no enrolment in an existing programme or promise of collaboration.
Share only what's needed to understand your idea. No medical records, debt statements, identity details or other sensitive information. Your name and other personal details are not needed.
No verified contact address has been configured yet. You can prepare your contribution here and save it locally. This page sends nothing and BOUW does not receive the file.

Follow BOUW
Follow ideas as they develop: from a proposal to a testable plan, and eventually to evidence and results. Including when an idea needs to change.
What you can follow
The work. And what we learn from it.
Proposals
Ideas for the Netherlands, open questions and changes when new knowledge calls for them.
Projects
The development of LOOP, GROW, HIVE, RISE and MEND. What do we want to build, what remains uncertain and what needs investigating first?
Experiments
When a plan is ready for a real test: the question, the method and what we want to measure. A research direction is not a pilot that has started.
Results
What was actually measured, with sources, limitations and the next decision. Setbacks, changes of direction and reasons to stop belong here too.
BOUW has no published pilot results yet. Experiments and outcomes belong here only when they actually exist and can responsibly be published.
